newsitem.title: USA: AOL stock jumps on Morgan Stanley bullish view.
newsitem.headline: AOL stock jumps on Morgan Stanley bullish view.

text.p: The stock of America Online Inc., the nation's largest provider of online services, jumped Friday after a Morgan Stanley analyst said the company planned to announce in a few weeks that it has 8 million subscribers.
The stock shot up $5.25 to close at $39.625 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was one of the most active issues.

Traders said the analyst, Mary Meeker, made the remarks and continued to strongly recommend buying the stock, after an America Online presentation at a Morgan Stanley software, services and networking conference in Phoenix, Ariz.
Traders said Meeker said Ted Leonsis, president of AOL Studios, gave an "upbeat presentation" at the conference.
"The news that they are close to 8 million subscribers, that is what's moving the stock," one trader said.
Meeker was not immediately available for comment.
An America Online spokeswoman confirmed that Leonsis spoke at the Morgan Stanley conference Thursday, but she did not have any details on his presentation, or what took place at the conference.
She said AOL has not made any announcements about its subscriber base, which is currently over 7 million.
"We announce every million and at the end of the quarter," said the spokeswoman for the Dulles, Va.-based company.
Traders said that Morgan Stanley had previously forecast AOL would have 8.2 million subscribers by the end of March.
